epithet.en: King of Uruk, two-thirds god and one-third man
epithet.da: Uruks konge, to tredjedele gud og en tredjedel menneske

1.modern-en: Introduced as the king who knew all things, built the walls of Uruk and carved his hardships on stone. His people complain that he leaves no son to his father and no bride to her husband, and the gods answer by creating Enkidu. Before they meet he dreams of something like Anu falling on his shoulders and of an axe, both too heavy to lift, and his mother reads them as a friend who will never leave him.
1.modern-da: Introduceres som kongen, der kendte alle ting, byggede Uruks mure og huggede sin møje ind i sten. Hans folk klager over, at han hverken lader sønnen blive hos sin far eller bruden hos sin mand, og guderne svarer ved at skabe Enkidu. Før de mødes, drømmer han om noget som Anu, der falder ned på hans skuldre, og om en økse, begge for tunge at løfte, og hans mor tyder dem som en ven, der aldrig vil forlade ham.

2.modern-en: When he comes at night to the bed spread for the bride, Enkidu blocks the door. They wrestle like bulls until the threshold breaks and the wall shakes; then Gilgamesh bends his knee and his rage cools, and Enkidu praises him as Ninsun's son.
2.modern-da: Da han om natten kommer til brudesengen, spærrer Enkidu døren. De brydes som tyre, til tærsklen brister og muren ryster; så bøjer Gilgamesh knæet, hans raseri køles, og Enkidu priser ham som Ninsuns søn.

3.modern-en: Takes Enkidu by the hand like a brother and resolves to kill Humbaba in the Cedar Forest. When Enkidu fears the guardian he answers that only gods live for ever and that a name can last. He has huge weapons cast, hears the elders' warnings but will not turn back, prays to Shamash in tears, and asks his mother Ninsun to pray for him.
3.modern-da: Tager Enkidu i hånden som en bror og beslutter at dræbe Humbaba i Cedertræskoven. Da Enkidu frygter vogteren, svarer han, at kun guder lever evigt, og at et navn kan bestå. Han lader vældige våben støbe, hører de ældstes advarsler, men vil ikke vende om, beder grædende til Shamash og beder sin mor Ninsun bede for ham.

4.modern-en: At the gate of the forest he urges the sick, frightened Enkidu on: forget death, fear nothing, and the brave man who goes first protects his companion. Together they reach the barrier.
4.modern-da: Ved skovens port driver han den syge, bange Enkidu frem: glem døden, frygt intet, og den modige, der går forrest, beskytter sin ledsager. Sammen når de frem til spærringen.

5.modern-en: Gazes at the cedars and the Cedar Mountain. On the road he asks the mountain for dreams and wakes at midnight from three of them, the last full of thunder, fire and death; Enkidu reads the second as a good omen. The tablet breaks off and resumes as they cut off Humbaba's head.
5.modern-da: Ser op på cedertræerne og Cederbjerget. På vejen beder han bjerget om drømme og vågner ved midnat fra tre af dem, den sidste fuld af torden, ild og død; Enkidu tyder den anden som et godt varsel. Tavlen brister og fortsætter, da de hugger Humbabas hoved af.

6.modern-en: Washes off the grime of battle. Ishtar offers to marry him; he refuses with a list of the lovers she destroyed. After he and Enkidu kill the Bull of Heaven he dedicates its horns to Lugalbanda and asks the people of Uruk who is the most splendid of heroes.
6.modern-da: Vasker kampens snavs af. Ishtar tilbyder at gifte sig med ham; han afslår med en liste over de elskere, hun har ødelagt. Efter at han og Enkidu har dræbt Himmeltyren, indvier han dens horn til Lugalbanda og spørger Uruks folk, hvem der er den prægtigste af helte.

7.modern-en: Hears Enkidu ask why the great gods hold council. In Shamash's words he is the friend who will mourn Enkidu, let his body go unwashed and roam the open country in a lion's skin.
7.modern-da: Hører Enkidu spørge, hvorfor de store guder holder råd. I Shamashs ord er han vennen, der vil sørge over Enkidu, lade sin krop gå uvasket og strejfe om på sletten i en løvehud.

8.modern-en: Weeps before the elders of Uruk for his comrade. When Enkidu's heart stops he covers his face like a bride's, roars like a lioness robbed of her cubs, tears out his curls and prepares rich offerings for the funeral.
8.modern-da: Græder for de ældste i Uruk over sin kammerat. Da Enkidus hjerte står stille, dækker han hans ansigt som en bruds, brøler som en løvinde, der har mistet sine unger, river sine lokker af og forbereder rige offergaver til begravelsen.

9.modern-en: Roams the open country afraid of his own death and sets out for Utnapishtim. He fights lions at the mountain passes, passes the Scorpion-men of Mashu and walks the Road of the Sun through twelve double hours of darkness to the Tree of the Gods, whose fruit is red stone. Shamash asks him why he runs; he answers that he wants to see the light.
9.modern-da: Strejfer om på sletten i frygt for sin egen død og drager ud mod Utnapishtim. Han kæmper med løver i bjergpassene, kommer forbi Mashus skorpionmænd og går Solens Vej gennem tolv dobbelttimer i mørke til Gudernes Træ, hvis frugt er af rød sten. Shamash spørger ham, hvorfor han løber; han svarer, at han vil se lyset.

10.modern-en: Arrives at the wine-maker's house in animal skins and tells her of Enkidu's death and his own dread. She tells him to enjoy what is given to mortals; he asks only the way. With Urshanabi he cuts poles, pushes across the Waters of Death and tells Utnapishtim of his journey.
10.modern-da: Kommer i dyreskind til vinkvindens hus og fortæller hende om Enkidus død og sin egen rædsel. Hun siger, at han skal nyde det, der er givet mennesker; han spørger kun om vejen. Med Urshanabi skærer han stager, stager over Dødens Vande og fortæller Utnapishtim om sin rejse.

11.modern-en: Hears the story of the Flood. Told to stay awake for six days and seven nights, he falls asleep at once and wakes to seven loaves that count the days. He is washed and given a fresh cloak, dives for the plant called The Old Man Becomes a Young Man Again, loses it to a snake while bathing, and weeps. He brings Urshanabi home and shows him the walls of Uruk.
11.modern-da: Hører historien om Syndfloden. Bedt om at holde sig vågen i seks dage og syv nætter falder han straks i søvn og vågner til syv brød, der tæller dagene. Han bliver vasket og får en ny kappe, dykker efter planten, der hedder Den Gamle Bliver Ung Igen, mister den til en slange, mens han bader, og græder. Han tager Urshanabi med hjem og viser ham Uruks mure.

12.modern-en: Grieves that the earth has seized Enkidu. Enlil and the Moon-god do not answer him; Ea has Nergal open a hole, and Enkidu's spirit rises. Gilgamesh insists on hearing the laws of the underworld, and weeps at what he hears.
12.modern-da: Sørger over, at jorden har grebet Enkidu. Enlil og Måneguden svarer ham ikke; Ea lader Nergal åbne et hul, og Enkidus ånd stiger op. Gilgamesh insisterer på at høre underverdenens love og græder over det, han hører.

epithet.en: Wild man shaped from clay, Gilgamesh's friend and brother
epithet.da: Vild mand formet af ler, Gilgameshs ven og bror

1.modern-en: Shaped by Aruru from clay on the open plain, covered in hair, grazing with the gazelles. He fills in the hunter's pits and frees the animals. After six days and seven nights with the courtesan the herds flee from him; he has lost his wildness but gained understanding, and longs for a companion.
1.modern-da: Formet af Aruru af ler på den åbne slette, dækket af hår og græssende med gazellerne. Han fylder jægerens grave til og befrier dyrene. Efter seks dage og syv nætter med kurtisanen flygter hjordene fra ham; han har mistet sin vildskab, men vundet forstand, og længes efter en ledsager.

2.modern-en: Learns to eat bread and drink beer, oils his body and becomes human. He guards the shepherds against lions. Told of the king's custom with brides, he enters Uruk, blocks Gilgamesh's door and wrestles him to a standstill, then praises him.
2.modern-da: Lærer at spise brød og drikke øl, salver sin krop og bliver et menneske. Han vogter hyrderne mod løver. Da han hører om kongens skik med bruden, går han ind i Uruk, spærrer Gilgameshs dør og brydes med ham, til ingen af dem kan mere, og priser ham så.

3.modern-en: Weeps when they become friends, as his love leaves him. He knows the Cedar Forest and warns that Humbaba's breath is death, but agrees to go in front, as the elders advise.
3.modern-da: Græder, da de bliver venner, fordi hans elskede forlader ham. Han kender Cedertræskoven og advarer om, at Humbabas ånde er død, men går med på at gå forrest, som de ældste råder til.

4.modern-en: Speaks to the great gate of the forest as if it could hear. Then he lies sick for twelve days, his hands weak and his arms paralysed, and asks to turn back; Gilgamesh talks him into going on.
4.modern-da: Taler til skovens store port, som om den kunne høre. Så ligger han syg i tolv dage med svage hænder og lammede arme og vil vende om; Gilgamesh overtaler ham til at fortsætte.

5.modern-en: Reads Gilgamesh's second dream on the road as a good omen: the mountain that falls is Humbaba, whom they will capture.
5.modern-da: Tyder Gilgameshs anden drøm på vejen som et godt varsel: bjerget, der vælter, er Humbaba, som de vil fange.

6.modern-en: Seizes the Bull of Heaven by its horns and tail. When Ishtar wails from the walls he hurls the Bull's member at her. After the feast he dreams.
6.modern-da: Griber Himmeltyren i hornene og halen. Da Ishtar klager fra murene, kaster han tyrens lem efter hende. Efter festen drømmer han.

7.modern-en: Dreams that the gods have decided he must die. Struck down by fever, he curses the courtesan; Shamash reminds him what she gave him, and he blesses her instead. He dreams of being led to the House of Dust, where the dead sit in darkness.
7.modern-da: Drømmer, at guderne har besluttet, at han skal dø. Ramt af feber forbander han kurtisanen; Shamash minder ham om, hvad hun gav ham, og han velsigner hende i stedet. Han drømmer, at han føres til Støvets Hus, hvor de døde sidder i mørke.

8.modern-en: Dies. Gilgamesh mourns him as his right hand, the hunter of wild donkeys and leopards.
8.modern-da: Dør. Gilgamesh sørger over ham som sin højre hånd, jægeren af vildæsler og leoparder.

9.modern-en: Gilgamesh weeps for him as he sets out alone, afraid of sharing his fate.
9.modern-da: Gilgamesh græder over ham, da han drager ud alene, bange for at dele hans skæbne.

10.modern-en: Remembered in Gilgamesh's grief: he lay six days and seven nights before he was given up for burial, and has turned to dust.
10.modern-da: Huskes i Gilgameshs sorg: han lå i seks dage og syv nætter, før han blev givet til graven, og er blevet til støv.

12.modern-en: Held fast by the earth, he cannot return until Nergal opens a hole. His spirit rises like a wind, embraces Gilgamesh and reluctantly tells what the dead endure.
12.modern-da: Holdt fast af jorden kan han ikke vende tilbage, før Nergal åbner et hul. Hans ånd stiger op som et vindpust, omfavner Gilgamesh og fortæller modvilligt, hvad de døde må udholde.

epithet.en: Temple girl of Uruk who brings Enkidu into the human world (named Shamhat in later translations)
epithet.da: Tempelpige fra Uruk, der fører Enkidu ind i menneskenes verden (kaldes Shamhat i senere oversættelser)

1.modern-en: Brought by the hunter to the watering place. She shows Enkidu her beauty and stays with him six days and seven nights, then invites him to Uruk and tells him of Gilgamesh's dreams.
1.modern-da: Ført af jægeren til vandstedet. Hun viser Enkidu sin skønhed og bliver hos ham i seks dage og syv nætter, inviterer ham så til Uruk og fortæller ham om Gilgameshs drømme.

2.modern-en: Shares her clothes with Enkidu, leads him by the hand to the shepherds and teaches him to eat bread and drink beer.
2.modern-da: Deler sit tøj med Enkidu, fører ham ved hånden til hyrderne og lærer ham at spise brød og drikke øl.

7.modern-en: Cursed by the dying Enkidu, then defended by Shamash, and finally blessed by Enkidu with lovers, gold and lapis.
7.modern-da: Forbandet af den døende Enkidu, forsvaret af Shamash og til sidst velsignet af Enkidu med elskere, guld og lapis.

epithet.en: Guardian of the Cedar Forest appointed by Enlil

3.modern-en: Described by Enkidu and the elders: his roar is a whirlwind, there is fire in his jaws and his breath is death. Enlil set him to guard the cedars as a terror to mortals.
3.modern-da: Beskrevet af Enkidu og de ældste: hans brøl er en hvirvelvind, der er ild i hans kæber, og hans ånde er død. Enlil satte ham til at vogte cedertræerne som en skræk for mennesker.

4.modern-en: Called out by the heroes at the forest gate.
4.modern-da: Udfordret af heltene ved skovens port.

5.modern-en: His path runs straight through the forest. The fight is lost from the tablet; it ends with his head cut off.
5.modern-da: Hans sti går lige gennem skoven. Kampen er tabt fra tavlen; den ender med, at hans hoved hugges af.

epithet.en: Goddess of love and war, daughter of Anu
epithet.da: Gudinde for kærlighed og krig, Anus datter

6.modern-en: Asks Gilgamesh to be her bridegroom. Refused and insulted, she goes to Anu and Antu, threatens them until Anu makes the Bull of Heaven, and leads the mourning when it dies.
6.modern-da: Beder Gilgamesh blive hendes brudgom. Afvist og forhånet går hun til Anu og Antu, truer dem, til Anu skaber Himmeltyren, og leder sørgeklagen, da den dør.

11.modern-en: Cries out like a woman in labour as the Flood drowns her people, and swears by her lapis necklace never to forget those days.
11.modern-da: Skriger som en fødende kvinde, da Syndfloden drukner hendes folk, og sværger ved sit lapishalsbånd aldrig at glemme de dage.

epithet.en: Survivor of the Flood, made immortal by the gods
epithet.da: Den, der overlevede Syndfloden, gjort udødelig af guderne

9.modern-en: The goal of Gilgamesh's journey: the son of Ubara-Tutu, who knows about death and life.
9.modern-da: Målet for Gilgameshs rejse: Ubara-Tutus søn, der kender til død og liv.

10.modern-en: Sees a stranger in his ferryman's boat. He tells Gilgamesh that nothing lasts for ever and that the day of death is not revealed.
10.modern-da: Ser en fremmed i sin færgemands båd. Han fortæller Gilgamesh, at intet varer evigt, og at dødens dag ikke åbenbares.

11.modern-en: Tells how Ea warned him through a reed hut, how he built the boat, rode out the storm and released a dove, a swallow and a raven, and how Enlil made him like the gods. He sets Gilgamesh the test of sleep and, at his wife's urging, reveals the plant of youth.
11.modern-da: Fortæller, hvordan Ea advarede ham gennem en sivhytte, hvordan han byggede båden, red stormen af og slap en due, en svale og en ravn løs, og hvordan Enlil gjorde ham lig guderne. Han sætter Gilgamesh på søvnens prøve og afslører på sin hustrus opfordring ungdommens plante.

epithet.en: Wife of the immortal flood survivor
epithet.da: Hustru til den udødelige, der overlevede Syndfloden

11.modern-en: Blessed with immortality beside her husband. She asks him to wake Gilgamesh and let him go home in peace, bakes a loaf for each day he sleeps, and asks what gift he will take back to his land.
11.modern-da: Velsignet med udødelighed ved sin mands side. Hun beder ham vække Gilgamesh og lade ham gå hjem i fred, bager et brød for hver dag, han sover, og spørger, hvilken gave han skal tage med hjem til sit land.

10.modern-en: Bars her door against the wild-looking stranger, then tells him that the gods kept life for themselves: fill your belly, wash, wear clean clothes, care for your child and make your wife happy. She sends him to the boatman Urshanabi.
10.modern-da: Slår slåen for sin dør mod den vildt udseende fremmede og fortæller ham så, at guderne beholdt livet for sig selv: fyld din mave, vask dig, gå i rene klæder, tag dig af dit barn, og gør din hustru glad. Hun sender ham til færgemanden Urshanabi.

10.modern-en: Tells Gilgamesh that he wrecked his own crossing when he smashed the sails, and has him cut poles five gar long to push across the Waters of Death.
10.modern-da: Fortæller Gilgamesh, at han selv ødelagde sin overfart, da han slog sejlene i stykker, og lader ham skære stager på fem gar for at stage over Dødens Vande.

11.modern-en: Leads Gilgamesh to wash and dress, is told by Utnapishtim that the crossing will hate him, sails with Gilgamesh, witnesses the loss of the plant, and is shown the walls of Uruk.
11.modern-da: Fører Gilgamesh hen for at vaske sig og klæde sig på, får af Utnapishtim at vide, at overfarten vil hade ham, sejler med Gilgamesh, overværer tabet af planten og får Uruks mure at se.

1.modern-en: Interprets her son's two dreams as the coming of a friend who will stand by him.
1.modern-da: Tyder sin søns to drømme som komsten af en ven, der vil stå ved ham.

2.modern-en: Praised by Enkidu after the wrestling match as the mother who raised Gilgamesh above all heroes.
2.modern-da: Prist af Enkidu efter brydekampen som moren, der løftede Gilgamesh op over alle helte.

3.modern-en: Dresses in her finery, climbs to the roof and asks Shamash why he gave her son such a restless heart.
3.modern-da: Klæder sig i sin stads, stiger op på taget og spørger Shamash, hvorfor han gav hendes søn et så rastløst hjerte.

3.modern-en: Appointed Humbaba to guard the Cedar Forest as a terror to mortals.
3.modern-da: Udpegede Humbaba til at vogte Cedertræskoven som en skræk for mennesker.

11.modern-en: Brings the Flood without taking counsel, rages that a mortal survived, is rebuked by Ea, and then makes Utnapishtim and his wife like gods.
11.modern-da: Sender Syndfloden uden at rådføre sig, raser over, at et menneske overlevede, irettesættes af Ea og gør så Utnapishtim og hans hustru lig guderne.

12.modern-en: Gives no answer when Gilgamesh begs him to raise Enkidu from the earth.
12.modern-da: Svarer ikke, da Gilgamesh beder ham løfte Enkidu op af jorden.

1.modern-en: Named by the courtesan as the god who loves Gilgamesh.
1.modern-da: Nævnt af kurtisanen som guden, der elsker Gilgamesh.

3.modern-en: Receives Gilgamesh's tearful prayer and Ninsun's offering before the journey, and answers with an oracle.
3.modern-da: Modtager Gilgameshs grædende bøn og Ninsuns offer før rejsen og svarer med et orakel.

6.modern-en: Receives the heart of the Bull of Heaven as an offering.

7.modern-en: Reproaches Enkidu for cursing the courtesan, reminding him of the bread, the clothes and the friend she gave him.
7.modern-da: Bebrejder Enkidu, at han forbander kurtisanen, og minder ham om brødet, klæderne og vennen, hun gav ham.

9.modern-en: Asks Gilgamesh why he is running, when he will not find the life he is looking for.
9.modern-da: Spørger Gilgamesh, hvorfor han løber, når han ikke vil finde det liv, han søger.

11.modern-en: Fixes the hour of the rain that starts the Flood.
11.modern-da: Fastsætter timen for den regn, der begynder Syndfloden.

epithet.en: God of wisdom and the deep waters
epithet.da: Visdommens og de dybe vandes gud

11.modern-en: Reveals the gods' plan to a reed hut so that Utnapishtim can build a boat, and afterwards rebukes Enlil for sending the Flood without counsel.
11.modern-da: Afslører gudernes plan for en sivhytte, så Utnapishtim kan bygge en båd, og irettesætter bagefter Enlil for at sende Syndfloden uden rådslagning.

12.modern-en: The only god who answers Gilgamesh: he tells Nergal to open a hole so that Enkidu's spirit can rise.
12.modern-da: Den eneste gud, der svarer Gilgamesh: han beder Nergal åbne et hul, så Enkidus ånd kan stige op.

epithet.en: Father of the gods, lord of Uruk

1.modern-en: Hears the people's complaint about Gilgamesh and tells Aruru to make his match.
1.modern-da: Hører folkets klage over Gilgamesh og beder Aruru skabe hans lige.

6.modern-en: Reminds Ishtar that she brought Gilgamesh's insults on herself, then makes the Bull of Heaven once she promises grain for the lean years.
6.modern-da: Minder Ishtar om, at hun selv pådrog sig Gilgameshs hån, og skaber så Himmeltyren, da hun lover korn til de magre år.

1.modern-en: Washes her hands, pinches off clay and shapes Enkidu on the open plain.
1.modern-da: Vasker sine hænder, kniber et stykke ler af og former Enkidu på den åbne slette.

epithet.en: Guardian of the mountains of Mashu

9.modern-en: With his wife he sees that Gilgamesh is two parts god, warns him that no one has crossed the mountains, and lets him take the Road of the Sun.
9.modern-da: Sammen med sin hustru ser han, at Gilgamesh er to dele gud, advarer ham om, at ingen har krydset bjergene, og lader ham gå Solens Vej.

7.modern-en: Seen in Enkidu's dream of the House of Dust, with the scribe of the underworld kneeling before her. She lifts her head and sees him.
7.modern-da: Set i Enkidus drøm om Støvets Hus med underverdenens skriver knælende foran sig. Hun løfter hovedet og ser ham.

12.modern-en: At Ea's command opens a hole in the earth so that Enkidu's spirit can rise and speak with his brother.
12.modern-da: Åbner på Eas befaling et hul i jorden, så Enkidus ånd kan stige op og tale med sin bror.
